summary: The Veteran Caregiver Reeducation, Reemployment, and Retirement Act expands support, medical coverage, and employment assistance for family caregivers participating in the Department of Veterans Affairs Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers. It provides extended medical coverage and employment help for 180 days after leaving the program, adds bereavement counseling, includes retirement planning services, and directs multiple federal studies on workforce re-entry and retirement options for caregivers.

affected_groups.effect: Receive extended medical coverage for 180 days post-program, access to employment assistance and fee reimbursements up to $1,000, retirement planning services, transition support, and bereavement counseling.
Must administer expanded medical, employment, and bereavement services, coordinate with other federal agencies, and conduct multiple feasibility studies and congressional reports.
Must partner with the VA to study and report on the feasibility of a returnship program to help primary caregivers return to the workforce.

key_provisions: Extends medical care coverage for primary family caregivers for 180 days after their designation ends, unless dismissed for fraud, abuse, or mistreatment, or if they are eligible for Medicare Part A.

Requires the VA to provide employment assistance to primary family caregivers during their active caregiving period and for 180 days following the end of their participation, including up to $1,000 in fee reimbursements for certifications or relicensure.

Provides primary family caregivers access to no-cost VA training modules for continuing professional education credits and connects them with employment assistance through the Departments of Defense and Labor.
Expands available support services to include retirement planning services and transition support during the 180-day period after leaving the program.
Mandates bereavement counseling and support for family caregivers following the death of a veteran receiving care under the program.

Directs the VA, in partnership with the Department of Labor and the Department of the Treasury, to conduct official studies and submit congressional reports regarding returnship programs, hiring former caregivers at VA facilities, and establishing retirement plans or savings pathways for caregivers.
Requires the Comptroller General to submit a report within two years assessing VA efforts to support family caregivers transitioning away from caregiving.
missing_information: The total estimated financial cost or appropriations required to implement the expanded benefits and studies.
The exact number of primary family caregivers who would become immediately eligible for the extended 180-day medical and employment benefits.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Veteran Caregiver Reeducation, Reemployment, and Retirement Act expands support, medical coverage, and employment assistance for family caregivers participating in the Department of Veterans Affairs Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers. It provides extended medical coverage and employment help for 180 days after leaving the program, adds bereavement counseling, includes retirement planning services, and directs multiple federal studies on workforce re-entry and retirement options for caregivers.
summary_detail.significance: The bill broadens the scope of federal support for family caregivers of veterans by bridging the gap between active caregiving and post-caregiver life. It addresses post-service employment, retirement, and medical transition periods that are currently unaddressed in federal law.
